fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"Banking At The Wheel's Hub","body":"Crutchfield traces his map back to a single sheet of paper sketched during a live stream and finished on an iPad on the way to Confluence 2025. It became the spine of Biopsy of a Psyop, a wheel with banking at the center and eight spokes: pharma, food, education, entertainment, technology, politics, history, and religion. Drawing on his decade of Los Angeles film work from 2010 to 2020, he argues these sectors quietly do each other's dirty work, pointing to pharmaceutical advertising money underwriting television. Garton highlights the summary line that ties it together, that the whole story is about how we categorize energy."},{"title":"Smart Dust And Full Spectrum Dominance","body":"The phrase biodigital convergence is not his own, Crutchfield notes, attributing it to the United Nations, the World Economic Forum, and standards bodies such as the IEEE, and linking it to Klaus Schwab's fourth industrial revolution and the claim that you are the technology. He describes a planned merging of biological and digital life, with blockchain acting as a translation layer, carried by pervasive grids of smart dust, particles he characterizes as specks with IP addresses and MAC identifiers. He cites full spectrum dominance, a stated goal in an early 2000s US Army manual, and argues ARPANET was built for this from its inception."},{"title":"Digital Middlemen And Human Servers","body":"Garton frames the endgame as middleman economics, an exponential new layer of tolls inserted between every organic exchange of energy, from breath to carbon to cellular function, plus enormous data sets harvested along the way. Crutchfield agrees and pushes further, arguing that today's data centers are a stopgap and the real aim is making each person the server that processes their own data, repaid in carbon credits or currency. Their sharpest illustration is hypothetical: if anyone could sit between your body and its own insulin, both men say, they would charge a subscription. The corporate move, Crutchfield adds, is to steal the real and sell back an imitation."},{"title":"Antenna Versus The Digital Twin","body":"Here Garton pushes back as a Biofield Tuning practitioner who reads human energy fields every week. Working from the hermetic idea that all is mind, he argues the biofield is not emitted by the body but forms it, closer to psyche than to hardware, so nothing can simply be written into it. Crutchfield concedes and sharpens his own claim: the biofield is only input and output, like a network card that moves data without processing or storing it, while the digital twin is what gets written to. He reaches for the two wine glasses demonstration, where rubbing one rim sets an identical untouched glass humming, as his picture of entrainment."},{"title":"Standards Bodies And Background Daemons","body":"Garton lays out the paper trail. The 802.15.6 wireless body area network standard, released in February 2012, describes using the living human body as the transmission medium; Thomas Zimmerman's personal area network research at MIT dates to 1995; and RAND's 2020 report on the internet of bodies catalogs devices that connect the body to networks along with what it calls governance gaps, which Garton reads as openings for gatekeepers. Crutchfield notes the standard sits two steps from Bluetooth, closer than Bluetooth is to Wi-Fi. Their tangent on computer daemons, background processes born when a parent forks a child, becomes a shared metaphor for the split-off psyche."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Chris Crutchfield joins InnerVerse to explain the ultimate conspiracy: the deployment of an internet of bodies that plugs your biofield into the grid. In his new documentary, "Biopsy of a Psyop, See," the six foot seven host of the 67 Podcast Chris Crutchfield drew the map that shows how banking sits at the dead center of a compartmentalized plan to digitize your biology, your biofield, and ultimately your soul, through what its architects call the biodigital convergence.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: We break down the IEEE 802.15.6 Wireless Body Area Network standard that treats the living human body as a transmission medium, and how it sits two iterations away from Bluetooth by design. We cover full spectrum dominance, transhumanism, smart dust, the digital twin, ARPANET, and Klaus Schwab's fourth industrial revolution claim that you are the technology. As a working Biofield Tuning practitioner, Chance questions whether anyone can truly write to the human biofield, drawing the line between the materialist science of bioelectricity and the consciousness that actually forms the field.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Hollywood Recruits, It Never Dictates", "body": "Chris describes an industry that does not hand anyone a script full of symbols. Talented artists get tapped, handed an NDA and a couple of things that are off the books, and the shadow people make sure the right project gets green lit. He watched it happen on a B.o.B. video in 2013, brought in for a rescue edit while the label's creative director pushed occult imagery that the artist, the director and the editor all disliked. Nobody had to say it out loud, because thirty grand and a second album were already on the line."}, {"title": "Modern Music as the Municipal Clock", "body": "Chris offers a hunch he has not heard anyone else state. If you are running a population like a computer network, it goes far more efficiently when everyone shares a clock. Quantized hip hop and EDM beats, perfect metronome timing blasted out over every FM antenna in a city, could produce a thermal, galvanic and piezoelectric similarity across the people who hear them. He compares it to buying an expensive external quartz master clock for a home studio so that every interface syncs to one source rather than to its own built in timing."}, {"title": "Music Inverted From Preserver to Corruptor", "body": "Chance traces the muses back to incarnations that open and close a world age, and notes that before writing was widespread, music was how information got preserved. That made music the savior preserver. Once recording and text took over the preservation job, the function came loose and flipped into its opposite. Chris fills in the production side with sigils drawn into the arrangement of tracks in a digital workstation, and John Todd's claim that Zodiac Records hired thirteen witches and thirteen warlocks to work a ceremony over every master before duplication, aimed at the subculture that would buy it."}, {"title": "Entertainment Is the Seeding Layer", "body": "Chance puts it plainly. Entertainment does not only sell drugs, it seeds ideas, because everything that gets built was an idea first. Chris fills in the plumbing from a decade in Los Angeles. A neighbor read seventy scripts a week for Warner to protect product placement deals. Aaron Sorkin's father sat on the Joint Chiefs and the dinner table became West Wing plots. A caterer overheard Brett Ratner say the United Nations was in his living room pitching a script it had already green lit, which reverses the entire order in which a film normally gets made."}, {"title": "Banking Is the Prototype for Everything", "body": "Chris closes the wheel he opened with. Banking belongs at the center because fiat gives that one point unlimited power to send toward whatever it wants to grow, and because accounting has always been a log of who did what when. That ledger is the prototype for the digital twin, a legal person that takes up no space but exists in time. Chance layers on Guenon, where time takes over space and quantity takes over quality, and money velocity governs how time feels, which is why lockdown dragged. Then come the accounts with thirty and eighty zeros."}]
